stem: Which statement about the isotopes of an element is correct?

options.A: They have the same number of protons and neutrons but different numbers of electrons.
options.B: They have the same number of protons and different numbers of neutrons.
options.C: They have different numbers of protons and the same number of neutrons.
options.D: They have the same nucleon number but different proton numbers.

stem: An atom has nucleon number 52 and proton number 24. Calculate the number of neutrons in the nucleus.
Which pair of species are isotopes of the same element?
Atoms of $^{40}_{18}\mathrm{Ar}$, $^{40}_{19}\mathrm{K}$ and $^{40}_{20}\mathrm{Ca}$ are compared. Which statement is correct?

options.A: They have the same number of electrons.
options.B: They have the same total number of protons and neutrons.
options.C: They have the same number of neutrons.
options.D: They are isotopes of the same element.

stem:
Which statements are correct when referring to the two common isotopes of chlorine?

1. The isotopes have different masses.
2. The isotopes have different numbers of nucleons.
3. The isotopes have the same chemical reactions.
An ion has nucleon number 49, proton number 20 and charge 2+. Calculate the number of electrons in the ion.
In the symbol $^{23}_{11}\mathrm{Na}$, what do the two numbers show?

options.A: 23 is the number of neutrons and 11 is the number of protons.
options.B: 23 is the nucleon (mass) number and 11 is the proton (atomic) number.
options.C: 23 is the proton number and 11 is the nucleon number.
options.D: 23 is the number of protons and 11 is the number of neutrons.

stem: How many protons, neutrons and electrons are in the ion $^{27}_{13}\mathrm{Al}^{3+}$?
A single $^{32}\mathrm{P}$ nucleus can be produced when a single $^{32}\mathrm{S}$ nucleus joins with particle X. In the process a proton is emitted. What is particle X?
Which property is the same for the isotopes $^{35}\mathrm{Cl}$ and $^{37}\mathrm{Cl}$?
Why do the isotopes of an element have the same chemical properties?

options.A: They have the same nucleon number.
options.B: They have the same number of electrons, giving the same electron configuration.
options.C: The extra neutrons take part in the bonding of the heavier isotope in the same way.
options.D: They have the same number of neutrons.

stem: Samples of gaseous $^{35}\mathrm{Cl}_2$ and $^{37}\mathrm{Cl}_2$ are compared at the same temperature and pressure. Which statement is correct?

options.A: They have different chemical properties but the same density.
options.B: They have the same chemical properties and the same density.
options.C: They have the same chemical properties but different densities.
options.D: They have different chemical properties and different densities.

stem: At the same temperature and pressure, $^{37}\mathrm{Cl}_2$ gas is denser than $^{35}\mathrm{Cl}_2$ gas. What is the best explanation?

options.A: $^{37}\mathrm{Cl}$ atoms have more electrons than $^{35}\mathrm{Cl}$ atoms.
options.B: $^{37}\mathrm{Cl}$ atoms have more protons than $^{35}\mathrm{Cl}$ atoms.
options.C: Each $^{37}\mathrm{Cl}_2$ molecule has a greater mass, and equal volumes of the two gases contain equal numbers of molecules.
options.D: $^{37}\mathrm{Cl}$ atoms have a different electron configuration, so they form stronger Cl–Cl bonds.

stem: A diatomic gas consists of molecules $\mathrm{X_2}$ in which each atom has a molar mass of 12 g mol$^{-1}$. Calculate the density of the gas at r.t.p., in g dm$^{-3}$. Take the molar volume at r.t.p. as $24.0\ \mathrm{dm^3\,mol^{-1}}$.
Which property is greater for $^{37}\mathrm{Cl}_2$ than for $^{35}\mathrm{Cl}_2$ at the same temperature and pressure?

options.B: the number of protons per molecule
options.C: the number of electrons per molecule
